name: Maryland
tagline: From Garrett County waterfalls to Smith Island, by way of canal towpaths, battlefields and crab towns.
intro: Maryland's byways run from the Allegheny plateau and the Potomac canal country through Civil War ground and Piedmont horse farms to the Baltimore harbor, the tobacco-and-church country of Southern Maryland and both shores of the Chesapeake. This chapter follows the Maryland Scenic Byways Program of the Maryland Department of Transportation State Highway Administration, which lists 18 byways covering about 2,487 miles; Visit Maryland publishes the route guides. Maryland byways are long, themed corridors with spurs and branches rather than single roads, and several have been renamed, merged or split over the years.

programs.label: Maryland Scenic Byways
programs.issuer: Maryland Department of Transportation State Highway Administration

members.name: Historic National Road
members.blurb: In Maryland the old National Pike runs 173 miles from Baltimore to the Pennsylvania line near Grantsville, past the toll gate house at La Vale and the single stone arch of the 1813 Casselman River Bridge.

members.name: Chesapeake and Ohio Canal
members.blurb: The road keeps company with the Potomac and the old canal towpath for 236 miles from Washington to Cumberland, by Great Falls, the Conococheague Aqueduct at Williamsport and the Paw Paw Tunnel, bored through 3,000 feet of rock.

members.name: Journey Through Hallowed Ground
members.blurb: The Maryland stretch of the Monticello-to-Gettysburg corridor runs 57 miles from Point of Rocks through Frederick to Emmitsburg, under Catoctin Mountain, where an iron furnace cast shells for Yorktown and a 78-foot falls drops into a gorge.

members.name: Antietam Campaign
members.blurb: From White's Ferry on the Potomac, 126 miles of country roads cross Civil War ground by Poolesville and Monocacy to Sharpsburg, where Tolson's Chapel, a log-and-frame church built by a Black congregation in 1866, stands near the Antietam fields.

members.name: Baltimore's Historic Charles Street
members.blurb: Charles Street climbs twelve miles north from the Inner Harbor to Lutherville, from the marble column of the Washington Monument on Mount Vernon Place out through Charles Village, laid out in the late 1800s as one of Baltimore's first suburbs.

members.name: Star-Spangled Banner
members.blurb: The route runs 106 miles from Hollywood in Southern Maryland to Edgemere, from Sotterley's old plantation house above the Patuxent to Fort McHenry, where a 42-by-30-foot flag still flew at dawn after a night of rockets and shells.

members.name: Booth's Escape
members.blurb: From Washington the route follows John Wilkes Booth's 1865 flight for 66 miles into Southern Maryland, past the Surratt tavern at Clinton and the Mudd farmhouse where a country doctor set the assassin's broken leg.

members.name: Religious Freedom
members.blurb: Across Charles and St. Mary's counties from Port Tobacco down to Point Lookout, the byway calls at St. Ignatius, a Jesuit parish founded in 1641, and at St. Mary's City, the colony's capital until 1695.

members.name: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad
members.blurb: Through Eastern Shore marsh and farm country between Cambridge and Goldsboro, 125 miles of roads pass the Blackwater refuge and the Bucktown store where a young Harriet Tubman was nearly killed for helping a man escape capture.

members.name: Mountain Maryland
members.blurb: Through the Garrett and Allegany highlands from Keysers Ridge to Cumberland, the byway wanders out to Swallow Falls and Deep Creek Lake, and to a boardwalk over the Cranesville bog, where carnivorous plants grow.

members.name: Old Main Streets
members.blurb: A 111-mile loop through the market towns of Frederick and Carroll counties, starting on Emmitsburg's late-1700s Main Street and coming back by the covered bridges at Loy's Station, Roddy Road and Utica Mills near Thurmont.

members.name: Falls Road
members.blurb: Falls Road climbs the Jones Falls valley out of Baltimore past stone mills that once sent their goods down the old turnpike and now house shops and homes, and through Bare Hills, a free Black community since the 1800s.

members.name: Horses and Hounds
members.blurb: A loop through Baltimore County hunt country, past Sagamore Farm, where the racehorse Native Dancer was kept, the clipped hedges of Ladew Topiary Gardens and the Worthington Valley fields of the Maryland Hunt Cup.

members.name: Lower Susquehanna
members.blurb: Thirty-three miles up one bank of the Susquehanna and down the other, from the decoy carvers' town of Havre de Grace over Conowingo Dam, where bald eagles and herons hunt, to Rodgers Tavern at Perryville.

members.name: Mason and Dixon
members.blurb: The byway keeps just south of the Pennsylvania line from Westminster to Appleton, past the 1797 Union Mills gristmill, where both armies stopped on the way to Gettysburg, and over Conowingo Dam to the Fair Hill turf course.

members.name: Chesapeake Country
members.blurb: From the canal town of Chesapeake City down the whole Bay side of the Eastern Shore to Crisfield, 419 miles past the water-driven Wye Grist Mill and crab towns, ending where boats leave for Smith Island.

members.name: Roots and Tides
members.blurb: Forty-seven miles down the Bay's western shore from Annapolis to Huntingtown, by the old port site of London Town at Edgewater and the forest and tidal marsh of the Smithsonian's research grounds.

members.name: Cape to Cape
members.blurb: Maryland's 79 miles of the Cape May to Cape Henry route, from Ocean City past Assateague's wild ponies and through Berlin and Snow Hill to the bald cypress along the Pocomoke River.
members.note: Route line from the state route layer (not in the 2022 national dataset).
